events.preview_text: Queue posts ahead and still slot in a same-day local update.
events.body:
With Buffer, you can line up a week of posts ahead of time and still drop in something that happened in the shop today.

Posting one at a time forces a trade-off. Plan nothing and you scramble for something to post; commit to a fixed run and it's awkward to interrupt when a timely local moment comes up.

Buffer is social media scheduling software for queuing Facebook and Instagram posts ahead of time. Your posts sit in a queue in the order they'll go out, and you rearrange them by clicking and dragging.

So when something happens today, you drag that post to the top and push the rest back — a drag, not a rebuild. It's the plan-ahead-yet-flexible way Foster Coffee works.

Before you build a weekly queue, it's worth checking the Free plan. It holds **10 scheduled posts per channel** at one time; once a post publishes, the slot opens again.

Take a look and see whether that fits the week you have in mind.
events.postscript: Reviewing the plan shows you the limit; setting up your posting times comes after you sign up.

events.subject: Line up the week, still post today
events.preview_text: A queue you can reorder with a drag when something happens in the shop.
events.body:
Plan a week of posts on a quiet Sunday, and by Tuesday something you didn't schedule happens in the shop.

A new pastry sells out, a regular brings their dog, the street fair gets a date. If your posts go out in a fixed order, slipping that in means moving everything behind it by hand.

Buffer is social media scheduling software for queuing Facebook and Instagram posts ahead of time. Your posts wait in a queue in the order they'll publish, and you reorder them by clicking and dragging.

So today's update doesn't cost you the plan — you drag it into place and the rest slides back.

Foster Coffee, a coffee company, works this way: planned far enough ahead to stay off the scramble for content, yet close enough that a last-minute change is just clicking and dragging posts around.

The Free plan holds **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time — a week on one channel, with room to spare. Before you build the queue, the official Free plan page lays out what's included, so you can see it fits your channels first.
events.postscript: The Free plan is free forever — it's not a trial, so there's no clock while you weigh it up.
